owasp_review.A01_access_control: PASS — subscriber resolved project-scoped via findByChat(projectId, telegramBotId, chatId); precedence query scoped by projectId+subscriberId. projectId is pinned upstream from the trusted rawUpdate, not attacker-supplied at this layer. No IDOR/cross-tenant path.
owasp_review.A03_injection: PASS — attacker-controlled message text is passed as matchKey and only used for an in-memory case-insensitive contains scan (Decision 3); Mongo criteria use parameterized .is(...) on exact literals (projectId, subscriberId, status), never the text. No NoSQL/query injection.
owasp_review.A04_insecure_design: PASS — keyword is a depth-0 human root (exempt from the volume rate-limit by design) but the dispatcher's Redis-independent fan-out ceiling (Decision 6c) bounds executions-per-firing; each message already passes the webhook's upstream controls. No new amplification.
owasp_review.A09_logging: PASS — keyword block logs ids/codes only (projectId + exception simpleName); the subscriber's message text is never logged (Decision 16 PII rule). No secrets/PII leak.
owasp_review.error_isolation: PASS — local try/catch(Throwable) scoped to the keyword block only; the worker's outer FAILED+rethrow path is untouched, so a genuine worker fault still surfaces and no security-relevant exception is masked.
